title: SoftBank: Execution of Follow-On Investment (Third Tranche) in OpenAI
content:
Execution of Follow-on Investment (Third Tranche) in OpenAI
SoftBank Group Corp. (“SBG”) today announced that, on October 1, 2026 (Japan time), it executed the third and final tranche of the follow-on investment (the “Third Tranche Investment”) in OpenAI Group PBC (“OpenAI”) via SoftBank Vision Fund 2, in the amount of USD 10.0 billion (JPY 1,579.6 billion*1) announced in “Follow-on Investments in OpenAI” dated February 27, 2026. Following the Third Tranche Investment, SBG has now completed the USD 30.0 billion follow-on investments in OpenAI previously announced. As a result, SBG’s cumulative investment in OpenAI totals USD 64.6 billion, and its ownership interest is approximately 13%. The Third Tranche Investment was funded with the proceeds from the issuance of foreign currency-denominated senior notes announced in “Issuance of Foreign Currency-Denominated Senior Notes” dated September 24, 2026.
Effective September 30, 2026, SBG canceled the remaining USD 10.0 billion of undrawn capacity under the bridge facility agreement entered into on March 27, 2026, with a total facility amount of USD 40.0 billion. Following this cancellation and the early repayment announced in “Early Repayment of Bridge Loans” dated September 9, 2026, all borrowings under the bridge facility agreement have been repaid and no undrawn commitments remain.

report.summary: SoftBank completes final $10B tranche of $30B OpenAI follow-on, bringing total investment to $64.6B and ~13% ownership.
report.background: OpenAI requires enormous capital for frontier-model training, compute infrastructure, and talent. SoftBank has been deepening its AI exposure through Vision Fund 2. In February 2026 it announced a $30B follow-on investment in OpenAI. To fund it, SoftBank arranged a $40B bridge facility in March 2026, then executed the first $10B tranche in April, the second in July, and the third in October. The final tranche was financed with proceeds from foreign-currency senior notes issued in September 2026. SoftBank also repaid and canceled the bridge facility, shifting from short-term bank debt to bond funding. Its cumulative OpenAI investment now totals $64.6B, giving it roughly 13% ownership.
key_points: SoftBank executed the third and final $10B tranche of its OpenAI follow-on investment on October 1, 2026, via SoftBank Vision Fund 2. This completes the $30B commitment announced on February 27, 2026.
SoftBank’s cumulative investment in OpenAI now totals $64.6B, and its ownership interest is approximately 13%. That makes SoftBank one of OpenAI’s largest outside backers.
The third tranche was funded with proceeds from foreign currency-denominated senior notes announced on September 24, 2026, replacing bridge financing with longer-term bond debt.

Effective September 30, 2026, SoftBank canceled the remaining $10B undrawn capacity under its $40B bridge facility. Following an earlier early repayment, all bridge borrowings are repaid and no undrawn commitments remain.
The sequence—bridge loan, three tranches, bond issuance, and facility cancellation—shows SoftBank structured a very large OpenAI commitment while managing near-term balance-sheet flexibility.
report.impact: The completed $64.6B investment reinforces OpenAI’s position as the best-capitalized private AI lab and signals that SoftBank sees frontier AI as a core strategic bet. For the AI industry, it raises the capital bar for competitors and may accelerate compute, model, and infrastructure spending. For developers, OpenAI may gain more capacity for APIs, tooling, and research, but dependence on a few mega-funders could shape product priorities and access terms. For regular users, better models and services may arrive faster, while concerns about corporate concentration, pricing, and safety governance persist. SoftBank’s ~13% stake also gives it significant exposure to OpenAI’s future valuation and commercial success.
report.tools: To follow this story, monitor SoftBank Group’s investor relations page for filings and bond documents, OpenAI’s official announcements, and SEC/EDGAR for related disclosures. Open-source finance tools like OpenBB and yfinance can help track SoftBank shares and AI-sector valuations. For deal data, Crunchbase and PitchBook are useful, though paid. Developers can watch OpenAI’s API changelog and platform docs to see whether new capital translates into model, pricing, or capacity changes.
